# Connectors: Summary

Azure Pipelines supports a wide number of connectors. These are listed and described on the [Azure Pipelines documentation](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/connectors/overview?view=azure-devops).


## Actions triggered by each connector

Each connector can support one or more triggers that start pipelines. The default actions are

 * `push`: triggered by changes in the source.
 * `pull request`: triggered when a pull request is created, updated or completed.
 * `work item`: triggered when a work item, like a bug or user story, is modified.

## Service connections

Some connectors invoke an API or make HTTP requests. These require a service connection. Learn more in the [Service connections](../taxonomy.md#service-connections) reference.

## Increased concurrency

If you want to run multiple pipelines at the same time:

- You can use the `pipelines` trigger on each individual pipeline.
- Use the `performace` triggers to control your pipeline runs.
- Lint the supported artifacts.
- You must have the appropriate permissions for the [Pipelines Concurrency feature]. Enterprise capacity can be configured using an administrator command for individual pipelines, [Pipelines Concurrency](../optimize/builds/concurrency.md#enterprise-concurrency).

 * [TFS](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/repos/tfs?view=azure-devops)
